c74object.name: jit.void.sm.writer
c74object.description:
jit.void.sm.writer writes numeric data from a Jitter matrix into a POSIX shared memory segment following the VOID Shared Memory contract (version 2).
The input matrix defines the shared memory topology. Matrix width corresponds to length and matrix height corresponds to channels. The matrix must be float32, single-plane, and two-dimensional.
Shared memory is created lazily. The first valid matrix received while the writer is enabled defines the structure of the shared memory segment.
Any structural change in the input matrix dimensions triggers a hard reset of the shared memory segment and increments the epoch value stored in the header.
This object is designed for deterministic inter-process data exchange and is symmetric with jit.void.sm.reader.

objarg.name: name
objarg.description:
Name of the POSIX shared memory segment to create.
Writers and readers must use the same name to communicate.

inlet.description:
Matrix containing the numeric data to write into shared memory.
The matrix must be float32, single-plane, with two dimensions. Width defines the number of samples per channel and height defines the number of channels.

outlet.description:
Outputs status messages describing the shared memory state.
Messages include connected and disconnected notifications emitted by the Max wrapper.

attribute.name: name
attribute.description:
Name of the shared memory segment.
Changing this attribute closes and destroys the existing shared memory segment if connected. The next valid matrix will recreate the segment using the new name.

attribute.name: connect
attribute.description:
Enables or disables the shared memory writer.
When enabled, the writer creates or updates the shared memory segment when matrices are received.
When disabled, the shared memory segment is invalidated and closed.

attribute.name: owner_project
attribute.description:
Project identifier written into the shared memory header.
This attribute is typically set automatically by the Max wrapper using the patcher filename.

c74object.details:
Shared memory layout consists of a fixed header followed by a contiguous array of float32 values.
Data is written in row-major order without padding.
Each write increments the frame counter stored in the header. Structural changes increment the epoch counter.
Readers use the epoch value to detect and handle layout changes safely.
